subject: Private Offer: Pricing & term approval request for Acme Corp (AWS Marketplace)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amal Malik <amal.malik@amazon.com>, Jessica Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme-corp.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private Offer: Pricing & term approval request for Acme Corp (AWS Marketplace)

Hi Amal / Jessica —

Thanks for the intro, Amal. Acme is ready to move from evaluation to paid production for a multi-service deployment (chat + embeddings + vector rerank). They asked us to submit an AWS Marketplace private offer to simplify procurement and centralize billing.

High level proposal (initial ask):
- 24-month private offer term
- Effective list-equivalent discount: ~22% applied against our standard hosted rates (detailed line items in the attached pricing_workbook)
- Payment: annual invoicing (Net 45) with additional option for quarterly invoicing if needed

Business rationale to justify term/discount:
- Predictable committed spend across multiple product modules (reduces unit cost)
- Willing to provide a co-sell case study + executive sponsor for joint GTM (adds measurable pipeline for AWS)
- Redwood will provide a 90-day onboarding services credit to accelerate deployment

Requests / asks:
1) Amal — can AWS create the private offer with the above term, and confirm buyer approval tiers we need to satisfy on Acme's side?
2) Jessica / Procurement — what internal approvals (procurement, legal, finance) and signatory cadence do you need to accept a 24-month private offer?
3) Vanessa / Karthik (cc'd) — please prepare a consolidated term sheet + pricing justification we can send to Acme procurement.

I attached a draft term sheet and the pricing workbook that breaks out yearly ARR and token assumptions. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pri*om.das@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: pricing_workbook.xlsx, Acme_Private_Offer_Term_Sheet.pdf

From: Amal Malik <amal.malik@amazon.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jessica Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer: Pricing & term approval request for Acme Corp (AWS Marketplace)

Priyom —

Thanks for outlining the ask. AWS can definitely create a private offer for Acme. A few things to note from the Marketplace operational side:

- Private offers are set up in the AWS Marketplace catalog; vendor must provide an effective price and term length.
- Buyer approvals: many enterprise buyers require procurement + legal signoff for terms >12 months or discounts above negotiated thresholds. For a 24-month commitment, Acme will likely need VP-level procurement/finance approval.
- Required artifacts from vendor: signed term sheet, PO template (we can accept DocuSign), and confirmation of the signatory authorized to bind Redwood.
- Timeline: once the private offer package is submitted it typically takes 2-5 business days for AWS to publish the offer and longer for buyer-side approvals depending on their internal cadence.

I'll attach the AWS private-offer process overview and can open a console request once we have the finalized term sheet. If you want, I can also route this to the Marketplace partnership desk to prioritize.

Best,
Amal Malik
Sr. Partner Manager, AWS Marketplace
amal.malik@amazon.com

Attachments: AWS_PO_Process.pdf

From: Jessica Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme-corp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Amal Malik <amal.malik@amazon.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-corp.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer: Pricing & term approval request for Acme Corp (AWS Marketplace)

Hi Priyom / Amal —

Thanks — a few clarifying questions from procurement before we pass to legal/finance:
1) Why 24 months vs 12 months? Our governance prefers 12-month base terms unless there is a clear ROI or price advantage.
2) Can you provide a year-by-year price breakdown and an explanation of the 22% effective discount? We need to present both list-equivalent and actual invoice numbers to our finance team.
3) Who will be the Redwood signatory? Acme requires vendor signatory name + title for the private offer.
4) Payment cadence: Acme prefers annual invoicing but may need Net 60 for enterprise customers. Can you absorb Net 60 or do you require Net 45?

I attached our standard SOW and procurement intake form. If you can provide the updated term sheet with these clarifications we can start routing internally.

-Jessica
Jessica Sullivan
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
j.sullivan@acme-corp.com

Attachments: Acme_SOW_v3.pdf

Subject: Fwd: Private Offer: Pricing & term approval request for Acme Corp (internal)

- Offer: 24 months with a 22% effective discount (breakdown in pricing_workbook.xlsx). Year 1: $420k; Year 2: $360k (assumes usage ramp-down).
- Rationale for 24-month term: lowers unit cost materially, offsets onboarding services credit we are providing, and secures co-sell commitment from Acme (marketing + exec sponsor).
- Payment: propose to accept Net 60 for this account given strategic value; finance will treat as slightly higher DSO.
- Signatory: Vanessa Ortiz, VP Sales (authorized signatory for marketplace private offers).

Asks:
1) Karthik — confirm finance tolerance for Net 60 and revenue recognition notes.
2) Marissa — approve a one-time commercial exception: 22% effective discount + Net 60. This exceeds standard discount caps for self-serve deals and requires leadership signoff.

(Quoted) — Jessica's note: 'Our governance prefers 12-month base terms unless there is a clear ROI or price advantage.'

Attachments: pricing_workbook.xlsx

Thanks,
Priyom
